newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Samper says former deputy "went off the rails".
newsitem.headline: Samper says former deputy "went off the rails".

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper compared his former Vice President Humberto de la Calle, who stepped down this month citing Samper's alleged drug ties, to a "pretty girl...who went off the rails."
In an interview with Argentine television channel America to be broadcast late on Wednesday, Samper criticised De la Calle for not speaking his mind when he was in government.

"It's like a girl who looks nice and pretty and like she's going to be a good wife and mother, who goes off the rails. That's what happened," said Samper, who replaced De la Calle with diplomat Carlos Lemos Simmonds.
"I'd have liked him to speak his mind in government, but not only did he not take an active role but what he has since expressed he never said while in government," said Samper.

De la Calle quit in protest at Samper's alleged ties to drug kingpins and charges that they helped finance his 1994 election campaign, amid what he called a deepening crisis of credibility in his government. He demanded that Samper join him in resigning -- a request Samper declined.
But Samper, cleared of any wrongdoing in his campaign by a congressional trial in June, is bent on seeing out his term.

Samper repeated his opposition to reinstating extradition but said he did not rule it out for the future. Terming it a "useful tool" in fighting drugs, he cautioned that Colombia took 10 years' intense debate to scrap extradition.
"Now's not the time to discuss it, because the government first wants to deal with projects on sentences and property which will allow us to fight organised crime," he said.
